# Generator-shortcuts answer

The strongest plausible rival is **`corner_fixed_vector`**: infer rotation from
the blue corner, but also memorize one displacement for each corner from the
canonical demonstrations—TL→(3,-1), TR→(3,4), BR→(2,4), BL→(-1,-4)—instead of
reading the green-to-orange vector. The executable rival fits all four canonical
training pairs exactly.

An exact disagreement is the canonical 11×13 test input retained in
`generators/7147e98f8173/counterexamples/corner_fixed_vector.json`. Its blue cell
is top-right, its green marker is `(0,1)`, its orange marker is `(2,4)`, and its
red staircase has bounding-box origin `(2,5)`. The intended displacement is
therefore `(2,3)`, not the memorized TR displacement `(3,4)`.

After one clockwise rotation, the normalized staircase cells are
`(0,1), (0,2), (1,0), (1,1)`. The intended rule places cyan at
`(4,9), (4,10), (5,8), (5,9)`. The rival instead places cyan at
`(5,10), (5,11), (6,9), (6,10)`.

I checked this three ways: the Python `rule_mirror` equals the canonical labelled
output; the selected Racket authority receipt is
`checks/repair/corner-fixed-vector-racket.json`; and
`test_strongest_canonical_shortcut_is_executable_and_refuted_by_query` verifies
4/4 canonical-train fits followed by disagreement on the test pair.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases deliberately. Its schedule includes
`same_corner_new_vector` and `same_vector_new_corner` profiles; in particular,
top-right appears with vectors other than `(3,4)`. Every query rotation in the
12 fixed-seed schedule lessons and all 2,400 rotations in the 300-lesson census
refuted the declared rivals without ambiguity.
